main_body: Tall Parisian-style townhouse: slate mansard roof with two dormers and a chimney, a red brick upper storey with lit windows and a balcony, and a shopfront with a striped awning at the bottom.
top_band: Rows 17-23 are a grey-blue slate band (L≈95-122) under a 1px dark outline. The scan shows no step of 25 L or more separating it from the slate below (L≈79-103), so it belongs to the same roof face and is not a separate top surface.
evidence: The whole building is drawn straight on. The mansard is a vertical slate face with dormers painted on it, and the grey band above it reads as a back parapet seen face-on, not a roof surface seen from above. The brick wall, windows, balcony and shopfront are all vertical faces. The orange cornice at rows 44-45 is a 1-2 row line with no visible top surface, and the windows are flat painted rather than inset. The Beodeul references show large lit roof slopes above their walls; this has no comparable surface, so it fails as a front elevation.

style.evidence: Brick, slate and window glow carry decent variation, with a median of 14 colours per tile (references 18 and 11) and 2% flat fill. But the candidate has only 56 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references, and 91% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references. The result is the neutral black outline of the sticker look, not the tinted material-tone outlines Beodeul uses. The slate roof and the upper rows are also fairly flat and repetitive, with fewer tonal steps than the reference roofs.
